flaws.description: The Stripe webhook handler parses the JSON body directly and never verifies the Stripe-Signature header, so anyone can forge a checkout.session.completed event and activate holds for free
Two concurrent POST /api/holds requests can both pass the check-then-insert and hold the same unit because there is no unique constraint or transaction serializing the check
Deposit and payment amounts are stored as float8 dollars, which loses precision and drifts from Stripe's integer cents
The webhook captures the payment before the database writes, so if the insert or update fails the tenant is charged with no refund or compensating step
Stripe retries webhooks, and the handler inserts a payments row and re-captures on every delivery with no idempotency check on stripe_event_id
The plan assumes the checkout.session.completed payload carries an expanded payment_intent with inline charges, but Stripe sends only the PaymentIntent id string and charges are not included
